title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. U/S is a relative hyperbolic curve, the complement in a proper smooth curve X/S of an étale divisor of cusps. Take a point s of S of codimension 1 and form the (non-strict) henselization Õ of O_{S,s}, with fraction field K̃.

One gets the exact sequence 1→π→E_{U_Õ}→E_Õ≅E_{k(s)}→1, which is canonically the sequence 1→π→E_{U_s}→E_{k(s)}→1 of the special fibre.

A rational section f of U/S, or more generally a section f̃ of U over K̃, gives:
- a section E_{f̃} of E_{U_K̃}→E_K̃;
- equivalently, a homomorphism λ: E_K̃→E_{U_Õ}≅E_{U_s} lifting E_K̃→E_Õ≅E_{k(s)}.

Here E_K̃ is the decomposition group N_{s'} of s' (the divisor of S at s) in Gal(K̄/K). It is an extension 1→I_s→E_K̃→E_{k(s)}→1 with I_s≅T=Ẑ(1) in characteristic 0 (or the tame part in general).

The page states that the following are equivalent:
- (a) λ is injective.
- (b) λ restricted to I_s≅T has the form k_i∘(μ·id_T). Here k_i: T→π is the canonical inertia embedding at a cusp i (up to π-conjugacy) and μ∈ℕ*.
- (c) λ|I is nontrivial.
- (d) the section E_{f̃} does not come from a section of E_{U_Õ} over E_Õ, i.e. λ does not factor through E_K̃/I=E_Õ.
- (e) f̃ is not regular, i.e. f is not defined at s.
- (f) the extension of f̃ to a section of X_Õ over Õ (valuative criterion, Õ a DVR) satisfies f̃(s)∈I=X_s∖U_s, the set of cusps.
Moreover, the cusp i in (b) is exactly f̃(s).

Implicitly, μ is the intersection multiplicity of the section with the cusp divisor. If t is a local equation of the cusp, f̃*t = unit·ϖ^μ, and Kummer theory gives inertia acting through μ times the cusp inertia.

In this cuspidal case the image of N_{s'}≅E_K̃ is a subgroup of E_{X_s} (by context presumably E_{U_s}) of finite index μ in the normalizer Ñ(L_i) of the cusp inertia L_i, i.e. the decomposition group of the cusp. The image of I is μT inside L_i≅T, and the map onto E_{k(s)} is the identity.

Purpose: this is part of the analysis of the section conjecture / anabelian description of rational points in families. A non-regular rational section produces a 'cuspidal' section of the special fibre's fundamental group sequence, landing in a cusp decomposition group. The next page continues: the only obstruction to a genuine lift is the factor I≅T, and any section of the extension of E_{k(s)} by T gives a cuspidal section of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)}.
errors: (b) only makes sense up to π-conjugacy, since k_i is defined up to conjugation; this is not stated.

I_s≅T=Ẑ(1) requires residue characteristic 0 (fine for S of finite type over Q, as the next page assumes). In positive or mixed residue characteristic one should use tame inertia and prime-to-p parts.
The page writes 'sous-groupe de E_{X_s}'. The cusp decomposition group lives in E_{U_s}; in E_{X_s} cusp inertia dies. This is likely a slip, or E_{X_s} is notation for the punctured situation.

The equivalences are stated without proof. They are correct: (c)⇔(d) since E_Õ=E_K̃/I; (e)⇔(f) by the valuative criterion; (c)⇒(a) since μ·k_i is injective on the torsion-free Ẑ(1) and the map is compatible with the identity on E_{k(s)}; (e)⇒(b) by a local Kummer computation at the cusp.

ideas.what: Specialization of a rational section across a codimension-1 point: a section over K̃ gives λ:E_K̃→E_{U_s}, trivial on inertia iff the section is regular at s.
ideas.modern_name: specialization of sections / sections over henselian DVR fraction fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore after Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings; developed by Nakamura, Stix (Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups, 2013)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) discusses sections and cuspidal phenomena; no explicit statement known to me

ideas.what: Non-regular rational section ⇔ inertia maps into the cusp inertia L_i via μ·k_i; the cusp is the specialization f̃(s) and μ is the intersection multiplicity.
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal (packet) sections, ramification index of a section at a cusp, tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (limit/tangential sections), Stix, Esnault–Wittenberg on cuspidal sections
ideas.where_published: Cuspidal sections are alluded to in the letter to Faltings; this quantitative form is not known to me in his published texts

ideas.what: Image of the decomposition group N_{s'} is a finite-index-μ subgroup of the cusp decomposition group (normalizer of L_i) in E_{U_s}.
ideas.modern_name: cusp decomposition groups as normalizers of inertia; index equals contact order
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix)

missed.claim: A clean six-way equivalence characterizing when a rational section of a relative hyperbolic curve fails to extend over a codimension-1 point, purely in terms of the induced map on decomposition/inertia groups. It includes the identification of the cusp and the multiplicity μ as an index. This is essentially the mechanism later used in the literature on cuspidal sections and specialization of sections, here written down by Grothendieck in the 'Longue Marche' period.
missed.quote: La restriction de cet homom. : I_s ≃ T est de la forme k_i ∘ (μ ∘ id_T) ... De plus, dans ce cas le i dans b) n'est autre que f̃(s).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority. It documents that Grothendieck explicitly analysed cuspidal sections arising from degenerating rational sections, with multiplicity, around 1981. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and pertinent to the section conjecture. However, the equivalences are by now standard in the literature on specialization and cuspidal sections (Nakamura, Stix). Interest is mainly historical, as an early explicit treatment with the multiplicity μ.
